la:noun:sella.gloss: seat, chair (one that is moveable unlike a sedīle)
senses: seat, chair (one that is moveable unlike a sedīle)
A kind of open or enclosed sedan chair
la:noun:sella.html:
sella (ancient collat. form sedda, acc. to Scaur. p. 2252 P.), ae, f.dim.
for sedla; root sed-; .sedes
,
a seat, settle, chair, stool (syn.: sedile, scamnum): viden' ut expalluit! datin' isti sellam, ubi assidat cito,; ; : scabilla, sellas, solia,; : in sellā sedere, (corresp. to sedes): fracta est patris sella,: altā deducere sellā,—
Esp.
Of a mechanic's work-stool: ipsum sellae atque operis et quaestus cottidiani locum,: in foro sellam ponere,.—
Of a teacher's chair, —
Of a portable chair or sedan (different from the lectica, a litter made like a bed): aut sellā, aut lecticā transire,; so (opp. lectica) ; ; ; simply sella,; ; ; called also sella gestatoria,; ; ; cf.: gestamen sellae,; .—
Of a seat in a coach or wagon, .—
Of a close-stool, ; ; also called sella familiarica,. —
Of a saddle, Cod. Th. 8, 5, 47; ; ; .—
Esp., a magistrate's seat or chair (very freq.), ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; also called sella curulis; v. curulis.—Prov.: duabus sellis sedere, to sit on two stools, i. e. to keep in with both parties, Laber. ap. ; id. ap. .

la:other:Selinus.html:
Sĕlīnūs, untis, f., = Σελινοῦς.
A town on the coast of Sicily, near Lilybœum, now Pileri: palmosa,; .—Hence,
Sĕlīnūsĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Selinus, Selinusian: creta,; ; .—
Sĕlīnuntĭi, ōrum, m., the inhabitants of Selinus, .—
A town on the coast of Cilicia, now Selinty, ; .—Also, a river near it of the same name, .

la:verb:seligo.gloss: to separate by culling out; pick or choose out, select, cull
senses: to separate by culling out; pick or choose out, select, cull
la:verb:seligo.html:
sē-lĭgo, lēgi. lectum, 3, v. a.
se-lego
.
In gen. separate by culling out; to choose out, cul select (rare but class.; syn.: eligo, deligo), nec vero utetur imprudenter hac copia (communium locorum), sed omnia expendet et seliget,: exempla,; Orell. and Otto N. cr.: ex quo (commentario) tu, quae digna sunt, selige, Cael. ap. ; ; : selectae sententiae,: (Romulus) selecta pectora Patres dixit,.—
In partic.
Judices selecti, the judges in criminal suits selected by the prœtor, ; ; ; ; : non potest ad haec sumi judex ex turbā selectorum,; cf. also .—
Di selecti, acc. to Varro, the following twenty Roman deities (twelve male and eight female): Deos selectos esse Janum, Jovem, Saturnum, Genium, Mercurium, Apollinem, Martem, Vulcanum, Neptunum, Solem, Orcum, Liberum patrem, Tellurem, Cererem, Junonem, Lunam, Dianam, Minervam, Venerem, Vestam, Varr. ap. , 7, 2 sq.; cf. , 7, 33. The sixteenth book of Varro's Antiquitates rerum divinarum treats of the di selecti; cf. Becker, Antiq. 4, p. 24 sq.
